scenes.title: Where and when
narration: Created in 1927 by Leonard Reed and Willie Bryant as 'Goofus,' the routine was a finale for the Whitman Sisters troupe.
It gained popularity in Harlem during the 1930s and was later adapted for the swing dance community by Frankie Manning in the 1980s.
on_screen: Map: United States · North America
Image — MISSING

scenes.title: When it is danced
narration: Originally a grand finale to invite all performers and staff to join in, it serves today as a communal ritual at the end of or during the height of swing dance parties.
Today it is a living tradition.
on_screen: Footage: File:Shim Sham at CCX 2022.webm (https://upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/9/93/Shim_Sham_at_CCX_2022.webm?utm_source=commons.wikimedia.org&utm_campaign=imageinfo&utm_content=original)

scenes.title: Watch it
narration: The dance consists of 32-bar choruses featuring four main steps: the Double Shuffle, the Cross Over, Tack Annie, and Falling Off a Log.
It is performed in a line formation, often transitioning into freestyle Lindy Hop once the choreographed phrases are complete.
Watch for Double Shuffle, Cross Over, Tack Annie.
on_screen: Hero video full screen, 30–45 s (268jUcVRdoY)
Captions name each signature move as it appears

scenes.title: Listen
narration: The dance is best suited for swing music with a medium tempo where the melody starts on beat eight.
'The Shim Sham Song' was written specifically for the routine, though modern swing dancers frequently use 'Tain't What You Do (It's The Way That Cha Do It)' and 'Tuxedo Junction'.
The pulse is 4/4.
Swing music with a medium tempo, featuring a melody that begins on beat eight to align with the choreography.

No specific costume is required, though it originated in the context of professional stage performance and social ballroom dancing.

scenes.title: The people
narration: Leonard Reed, Willie Bryant, Frankie Manning, Al Minns, Leon James, Dean Collins, Howard 'Stretch' Johnson.
Variations include the original 1927 routine, the 'Freeze Chorus,' the 'Joe Louis Shuffle Shim Sham,' the 'Savoy Shim Sham,' and the 'Revenge of the Shim Sham.'
The routine evolved from a professional tap finale into a global swing line dance.
